dominantMode: Evaluating responses and management strategies for sustainability, at a range of scales, incorporating multiple perspectives and geographical data
cleanRule: Geography (2022 syllabus) answers are marked on geographical reasoning about places, environments and change: a high-band evaluate/assess response must judge responses or management strategies for sustainability, at a range of scales, using evidence, geographical concepts (place, space, environment, interconnection, scale, sustainability, change) and — where the directive requires — multiple perspectives. Describing a strategy without judging its effectiveness for sustainability does NOT meet an evaluate/assess directive.
leaderboardTip: Geography rewards judgement, not description: evaluate/assess management strategies for sustainability AT A RANGE OF SCALES, and bring in different perspectives and geographical data.

bandRules.Band6: Extensive knowledge and understanding of geographical concepts; evaluates responses and management strategies, at a range of scales, for sustainability; synthesises and interprets complex geographical data and information for patterns, trends and relationships and to support investigation; proposes well-developed explanations for and responses to geographical challenges and opportunities in different and unfamiliar contexts; applies an extensive range of geographical skills and tools; plans and conducts sophisticated geographical inquiry including fieldwork; communicates logically and effectively using precise geographical terms in a variety of forms and contexts.
bandRules.Band5: Thorough knowledge and understanding; assesses responses and management strategies, at a range of scales, for sustainability; interprets complex geographical data for patterns, trends and relationships; proposes explanations for and responses to challenges and opportunities in different and unfamiliar contexts; applies a range of geographical skills and tools; plans and conducts well-developed geographical inquiry including fieldwork; communicates logically and clearly using appropriate geographical terms.
bandRules.Band4: Sound knowledge and understanding; explains responses and management strategies, at different scales, for sustainability; interprets geographical data to show patterns, trends and relationships; proposes responses to challenges and opportunities in different contexts; uses a range of geographical skills and tools; plans and conducts sound geographical inquiry including fieldwork; communicates using appropriate geographical terms in different forms and contexts.
bandRules.Band3: Basic knowledge and understanding; outlines responses and/or management strategies for sustainability; identifies patterns or trends from geographical data; proposes basic responses to challenges and/or opportunities; uses geographical skills and tools; plans and/or conducts geographical inquiry including fieldwork; communicates using some appropriate geographical terms.
bandRules.Band2: Limited knowledge and understanding; identifies aspects of management strategies for sustainability; identifies basic geographical data; identifies responses to challenges and/or opportunities; limited use of geographical skills and tools; conducts basic geographical inquiry; communicates using basic geographical terms.
bandRules.Band1: Minimum standard expected was not demonstrated.

evaluate.subjectNote: In Geography, 'evaluate' asks for a judgement about responses or management strategies for sustainability, at a range of scales — their effectiveness/worth against criteria — supported by geographical data and, where relevant, differing perspectives. Naming or describing a strategy without judging it for sustainability does NOT satisfy 'evaluate'. A criteria-referenced verdict with modality is required.

assess.subjectNote: 'Assess' requires a judgement of value/effectiveness — of geographical challenges and opportunities, perspectives, or management strategies — with reasons and geographical evidence. Consider a range of scales where relevant.

analyse.subjectNote: 'Analyse' requires identifying components and relationships — spatial patterns, trends, interconnections, causes and effects of change in places and environments — and drawing out their geographical implications, using data where provided.

explain.subjectNote: 'Explain' requires relating how/why — geographical processes and influences that form and transform places and environments — using causal connectives and geographical concepts, not just description.

account.subjectNote: 'Account for' requires reasons/causes for a geographical pattern, process or change — a causal explanation, not a description of what is observed.

compare.subjectNote: 'Compare' requires identifying similarities AND differences between places, environments or strategies — use contrast connectives (whereas, in contrast) and geographical criteria.

subjectContext.examStructure: HSC written exam (2022 syllabus, first examined 2025): four sections, 100 marks, all compulsory. Section I — 15 multiple-choice (often stimulus/skills based). Section II — short answer. Sections III & IV — extended response. A minor revision to the Section III rubric applies from the 2026 HSC.
subjectContext.markingSpine: Year 12 outcomes centre on analysing places/environments and change (GE-12-01/02), assessing opportunities, challenges and perspectives (GE-12-03), and evaluating responses and management strategies for sustainability at a range of scales (GE-12-04/05). High-band answers judge strategies for sustainability across scales with data and perspectives — not description.
subjectContext.geographyNote: Reward use of the seven geographical concepts, explicit reference to a RANGE OF SCALES (local→global), and integration of geographical data/stimulus where provided. Evaluate/assess questions require a judgement about sustainability, not a recount of the strategy.
